item.title: AI Code's Bad Patterns Self-Replicate: 3 Instances Become 30, Silently
item.description: AI code decay isn't about 'low quality' — it's a structurally different kind of technical debt. Models treat your codebase as a style guide and faithfully replicate whatever patterns they find, including the wrong ones. A human team catches a bad pattern at 3 instances; AI silently propagates it to 30.

item.title: Cursor's Bill Disappeared. The Official Answer: Deliberate Design.
item.description: On July 31st, Cursor quietly removed dollar amounts from its usage page, zeroed out API cost fields, and an official employee confirmed it was 'deliberate design.' Meanwhile, real benchmark data shows token consumption varies 30x across agent harnesses. This isn't a UI change — it's a business signal.

item.title: llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang: Three Inference Engines, Three Completely Different Paths
item.description: llama.cpp, vLLM, and SGLang aren't competitors in the same lane — they're built on entirely different design assumptions. Which one fits your workload? The answer depends on one metric you probably haven't measured.
